leads.title: Senegalese Penal Code, Article 319
leads.documents: Criminalization of same-sex sexual activity; defines 'improper or unnatural act with a person of the same sex' as punishable.
leads.detail: Quoted in French and English in article: imprisonment 1 to 5 years and fine 100,000 to 1,500,000 francs; maximum penalty always applied if act with minor under 21. No URL visible.

leads.title: 2026 law lengthening penalties for 'unnatural acts' - Sonko bill adopted March 12, signed by President Bassirou Diomaye Faye March 30
leads.documents: New legal status: 5 to 10 years prison for 'unnatural acts', fines 100,000 to 10 million CFA francs vs 1.5 million prior, ban on 'promotion, financing and support of homosexuality, bisexuality and transsexuality', penalty for 'abusive relationships conducted in bad faith'; June 2026 constitutional amendment banning same-sex marriage.
leads.detail: Presented 25 February 2026 by Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko as campaign promise; adopted March 12; signed March 30 2026 and published in official gazette following day; June 2026 National Assembly voted unanimously to amend Constitution. No URL visible.

leads.title: United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights statement by Volker Türk
leads.documents: Institutional rights assessment that the new 2026 law violates human rights.
leads.detail: Cited as: According to UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, Volker Türk, the new law violates human rights. No URL visible.

leads.title: U.S. Department of State 2011 Human Rights Report on Senegal
leads.documents: Government report on criminal prosecution, widespread discrimination, social intolerance, acts of violence; media failure to report anti-LGBT hatred/violence; drop in reported cases due to going underground, international attention, legal challenges.
leads.detail: Long block quote reproduced in article; also cites July 2011 State Dept information on adoption eligibility. No URL visible.

leads.title: U.S. Department of State 2012 Human Rights Report on Senegal
leads.documents: Government report on 2012 enforcement: arrest, discrimination, police harassment including arrest on second-hand reports and poor treatment in detention; January arrest of two women over kissing video; October Dakar court sentence.
leads.detail: Quotes: Tasmir Jupiter Ndiaye sentenced to 4 years + 200,000 CFA francs ($400) for 'acts against nature' plus arms/battery; Matar Diop 3 years. Women held then released on bail, never formally charged. No URL visible.

leads.title: Human Rights Watch - 'Fear for Life: Violence against Gay Men and Men Perceived as Gay in Senegal' (November 2010)
leads.documents: Human-rights report documenting cases of violence against gay men 2009 and earlier and legal/cultural milieu fostering violence.
leads.detail: Cited via U.S. State Dept 2011 Report summary in article: 'In November 2010 Human Rights Watch released a report entitled Fear of Life...' No URL visible.

leads.title: Panos Institute West Africa report (released 20 July)
leads.documents: Finding that local media contributed to negative societal attitudes toward LGBT persons.
leads.detail: Cited via U.S. State Dept 2011 Report: 'A report by the Panos Institute West Africa released on 20 July found that local media contributed...' No URL visible.

leads.title: United Nations Human Rights Council Universal Periodic Reviews of Senegal (2009 and 2013)
leads.documents: Rights machinery: recommendations to amend Penal Code to decriminalize, end prohibition, release prisoners, moratorium on Article 319, anti-discrimination and dialogue; Senegal's refusal/defense citing culture, religion, social cohesion.
leads.detail: Lists recommending states (UK, Belgium, Canada, Netherlands, Slovenia, Czech Republic, Ireland, Uruguay, Argentina, Austria, Germany, Mexico, Brazil, Greece, Paraguay, Thailand, Switzerland); Senegal responses summarized plus statements by Foreign Minister Madické Niang 6 February 2009 and Justice Minister Sidiki Kaba 21 October 2013: 'There is no criminalization of homosexuality... Article 319 talks about acts contrary to nature.' No URL visible.

leads.title: United Nations Working Group on Arbitrary Detention - March 2010 finding
leads.documents: Finding that Senegal National Police detained persons alleged to have committed 'unnatural sexual acts'; recommendation on detentions for decency/public morality.
leads.detail: Quoted recommendation: 'Pay particular attention to detentions on the grounds of offending decency or public morality, with a view to avoiding any possible discrimination against persons of a different sexual orientation'. No URL visible.

leads.title: Ferguson, Jason L. (August 2021) - 'There Is an Eye on Us': International Imitation, Popular Representation, and the Regulation of Homosexuality in Senegal - American Sociological Review 86(4):700-727
leads.documents: Academic analysis of regulation of homosexuality in Senegal, international imitation and popular representation.
leads.detail: Listed in Further reading with citation detail: doi:10.1177/00031224211026546. No other URL visible.
